DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Davidson Day School
CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER
AFAR Archaeology & Global Studies
Davidson, North Carolina • Patriots • Lake Norman Region
Davidson Day’s flagship non-athletic program: a pre-collegiate international archaeological field-research
and cultural-site-preservation program, paired with a research-driven Global Studies Diploma.
AFAR — American Foreign Academic Research Program
AFAR conducts full-scale international archaeological field research and cultural site preservation with
pre-collegiate students. The program was founded in 2006 and takes roughly 60–70 students to active
excavation sites each summer. Coverage has described it as one of only two field schools in the United States
that takes high school students on an international dig.
What students do
Students work alongside professional archaeologists at active excavation sites, with evening and weekend
lectures and cultural excursions built around each location. Methods documented in the program include
hands-on excavation and ground-penetrating radar survey.
Field sites (documented)
• Cahal Pech, Belize — a long-running site; 2026 is noted as the 20th year of work there.
• Zorita de los Canes castle, Spain — an 11th field season is noted for summer 2026.
• Tróia (Roman city), Portugal — work documented since 2018.
• Mieza, Greece — work documented since 2017.
• North Carolina (Wachovia / Winston-Salem) — in November 2024, AFAR students worked with the North
Carolina State Historic Preservation Office at the Adam Spach Rock House excavation, using
ground-penetrating radar and excavation methods.
Recognition & scholarly presentation
AFAR Archaeology & Global Studies Page 1
DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Students present field research at collegiate-level archaeology conferences. The school has documented a
group of AFAR students traveling to present their research at the Mount Royal University Archaeology
Conference in Calgary, with at least one student presenting in multiple consecutive years. The school frames
the opportunity to present original field research at a collegiate conference as distinguishing the program from
most others.
Field Detail
Program type Pre-collegiate international archaeological field research & site preservation
Founded 2006
Grade levels Grades 7–12 (Middle & Upper School); deepest engagement in Upper School
Scale ~60–70 pre-collegiate students annually
Sites Belize, Spain, Portugal, Greece, and North Carolina
Scholarly output Student presentations at a collegiate archaeology conference
Global Studies Diploma Program
The Global Studies Diploma is a special-diploma distinction that pairs field-based research with international
coursework and a capstone. It is closely linked to AFAR, though field research can also be satisfied through an
approved project.
Documented requirements & components
• A minimum of two weeks of international field research (via AFAR or an approved project).
• International / globally focused coursework.
• A capstone research project, paper, and public presentation at the Davidson Day Scholars Research
Conference.
• Language study.
• An internship, volunteer, or pre-collegiate requirement of at least 100 hours.
• A supporting lecture and workshop series, plus program travel.
Scope & sourcing note
Site-by-site details and season counts reflect the school’s own published program descriptions and
regional coverage. Individual program directors, advisors, and student participants are intentionally omitted
per dossier policy. No comparisons to any other school’s programs are drawn.
AFAR Archaeology & Global Studies Page 2

sections.text:
# Davidson Day — Clubs — Club Catalog & Overview

Research Area — Scope, honest gaps, and the clubs confirmable from public sources.

+ page fetches). Prior Davidson Day dossiers organized student life thematically
(AFAR, Academic Recognition, Service, Traditions) with no catalog/roster section, so
this file adds the missing catalog view. Nothing here is inferred or invented.

**Honesty caveat (important).** Davidson Day does NOT publish a public, enumerated
roster of named student clubs on its own site (davidsonday.org). Every division and
student-life page frames activities through programs, councils, and traditions — the
Community Engagement Councils and Patriot Week service framework, the Student Diversity
Council, the Middle School House System, Patriot Pals, the AFAR archaeology
field-research program, and the Global Studies Diploma — rather than an interest-club
list. A real activities list likely lives behind the login-gated Patriot Connect /
parent portal, which could not be accessed.

**Verdict:** PARTIAL — no roster on the school's own site; one named list exists only
on the third-party aggregator PrivateSchoolReview (single-source, undated, no division
breakdown, and uncorroborated against the school).

**Named clubs (single source: PrivateSchoolReview, unverified by the school).**
PrivateSchoolReview lists 17 extracurriculars with no division breakdown. Applying the
series scope (non-athletic, non-fine-arts student clubs), the confirmable interest and
academic clubs are: Chess Club, Debate Club, Science Club, Math Olympiad, Environmental
Club, Outdoor Club, Creative Writing Club, Film Club, and Community Service Club.

**Excluded.** Art, Guitar, and Photography clubs are excluded as fine-arts; Student
Government Association, Honor Council, and the Student Ambassador Program are governance
bodies or programs, not interest clubs; Rowing is athletic; Battle of the Books is the
Middle School reading-competition team covered in the Academic Recognition & Competition
dossier.

**Not clubs — documented on davidsonday.org, correctly excluded.** Community Engagement
Council (CEC), Middle School Service Days, service-learning (service framework); Patriot
Pals (mentorship tradition); House System / House Cup (Middle School tradition); Student
Diversity Council (council); AFAR archaeology and the Global Studies Diploma (academic
programs); Revolution yearbook, theatre, and show choir (arts / publications).

**Gaps / login-gated.** No school-hosted club roster found; candidate URLs 404. A real
activities list likely lives in the login-gated Patriot Connect / Veracross-style
parent-student portal, which was not fetchable. PrivateSchoolReview names are
uncorroborated. Niche returned HTTP 403; U.S. News timed out — neither confirmed.

**Honest position:** no official club count is asserted. The clubs above are reported as
aggregator-listed and unverified; the school's own documented structures are programs
and councils, not a club roster.

Source: PrivateSchoolReview — Davidson Day School profile (privateschoolreview.com/davidson-day-school-profile; single-source, unverified). Davidson Day School — Upper School, Middle School, and Community & Culture pages (davidsonday.org). Wikipedia — Davidson Day School.

---

Belonging & Inclusion Advisory Committee

diversity and inclusion initiatives. It is the standing cross-constituency body in this area and includes Upper

DAVIDSON DAY SCHOOL CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Davidson Day School
CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER
Service & Community Engagement
Davidson, North Carolina • Patriots • Lake Norman Region
A JK–12 community-engagement framework anchored by divisional and Upper School student-leadership
councils, a week-long service tradition, and required Middle School service-learning.
Structure
Davidson Day organizes service through a school-wide framework that has engaged students in the community
since the early 2000s. Day-to-day work runs through divisional councils and an Upper School
student-leadership council.
Councils & programs (confirmed)
• Center for Community Engagement — the JK–12 framework coordinating service across divisions.
• Patriot Community Engagement Councils (PCECs) — divisional service groups in which students and
faculty collaborate to develop high-impact service projects.
• Community Engagement Council (CEC) — an Upper School student-leadership service group; one
documented effort had a group of Upper School CEC students raising money to fund four local nonprofits.
• Patriot Week — a signature service tradition of seven-plus days of service in April, engaging JK–12
students, families, and faculty with community nonprofits.
• Middle School service-learning — every Middle School student takes part in a hands-on service-learning
program partnering with local organizations; the school also runs Middle School Service Days.
• Community Engagement Summit & Nonprofit Fair — school-hosted events connecting Middle and Upper
School students with nonprofit volunteer opportunities.
• Patriot Pals — a cross-divisional mentoring tradition pairing an Upper School student with a Lower School
student for the year (community-building / service overlap).
Service & Community Engagement Page 1

Davidson Day channels student leadership through service and affinity councils rather than a traditional

Davidson Day publishes **no named affinity/identity groups** — no Black Student Union,
Asian Student Alliance, GSA, Latine affinity group, or equivalent. There is no DEI nav
item; the school's framing is "**Belonging**," not affinity.

### What does exist — VERIFIED

All from https://www.davidsonday.org/student-life/belonging. These three bodies are
**councils and committees, not affinity groups**:

| Body | Type | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Student Belonging Council** | Student-led | "Developed by students… started hosting monthly belonging forums in **2020**. Advances conversations about diversity, community, and belonging at Davidson Day and beyond." |
| **Upper School Belonging Council** | Student, Upper School | Leadership plus faculty sponsor **Steve McGill**; featured on the Davidson Day Community Podcast with Head of School Andrew Bishop. |
| **Belonging Committee** | Adult (administrators, faculty, staff) | Meets **monthly**; implements belonging initiatives, addresses strategic-plan goals, organizes professional development, guided development of the Statement of Belonging. |

**Forum topics** — event themes, **not** standing groups: The African-American Student
Experience · The LGBTQ+ Experience · Disability Awareness Forum · The Immigrant Experience ·
Mental Health Forum.

**Statement of Belonging** (verbatim): "Davidson Day School is committed to maintaining a
welcoming, supportive learning environment that values belonging. We respect individual
differences in ethnicity, gender, national origin, race, color, religion, sexual
orientation, ability, and socioeconomic status."

### Why the card is omitted

- **No enumerated affinity-group roster by name** anywhere on the site. The 1a card is an
 ecosystem map built from a named roster; with no roster there are no cells to draw.
- **No division breakdown** — only Upper School is named; no Lower/Middle School groups.
- **No parent affinity groups.** The only two parent orgs are the **Patriot Parent
 Association (PPA)** and the **Patriot Athletic Club (PAC)** — social and athletic, neither
 identity-based. → https://www.davidsonday.org/get-involved/parent-organizations
- **No student diversity leadership arm**; no NAIS SDLC attendance published anywhere.
- **No count discrepancy to flag** — no page publishes any count at all.

sections.text:
This is the one area with real, citable substance.

### Program 1 — Diploma Distinctions Practicum — scale: minimum 100 hours

Every Diploma Distinction requires an "Immersive Practicum (Minimum 100 Hours)" —
internships, civic engagement, nonprofit leadership, medical shadowing, or pre-collegiate
programs. Students apply at the end of sophomore year, and the track adds quarterly
**Ethics Labs** and a capstone at the **Davidson Day Scholars Research Conference**. The
**Business and Civic Engagement Diploma** specifies "At least 100 hours of an approved
internship, volunteer opportunity, or pre-collegiate program."

**Important qualifier:** this is an **opt-in diploma track**, *not* a school-wide graduation
service requirement.

- Sources: https://www.davidsonday.org/academics/diploma-distinctions ·
 https://www.davidsonday.org/academics/diploma-distinctions/business-civic-engagement

### Program 2 — Davidson College Deliberative Citizenship Initiative — scale: 13 students; first high school ever to partner

Davidson Day is "the first high school to collaborate with this program." Thirteen Upper
School students completed two deliberation modules — "Balancing Liberty and General
Welfare: The Case for Social Safety Nets" and "Justice and the Rule of Law: The Case for
Constitutional Rights" — attending expert panels and two-hour small-group deliberations
centered on civil discourse rather than debate-to-win.

- Source: https://www.davidsonday.org/p/~board/all-blogs/post/learning-to-disagree-better
- **"Not a club" label:** this is a structured partnership/program, not a standalone club.

### Program 3 — Middle School Service Learning — scale: 100% of Middle School students

"Every Middle School student takes part in our hands-on service-learning program,
partnering with local organizations." Service Days: "every student actively participates in
dedicated days of service throughout the year." No hour count, partner count, or founding
year is published.

- Sources: https://www.davidsonday.org/academics/middle-school ·
 https://www.davidsonday.org/student-life/community-and-culture

### Also confirmed — Upper School Community Engagement Council

Described as demonstrating "a deep commitment to service and leadership by creating
meaningful opportunities for students to make a positive impact both locally and beyond."
**No scale number, roster, or founding year published**, and its "Learn More" link is dead.
→ https://www.davidsonday.org/student-life/community-and-culture

### Community partnerships — 8 named — VERIFIED

Champions House of Care · The Kindness Closet · Food for Days · Beds for Kids · American
Foreign Academic Research (AFAR) · Davidson Public Library · Davidson College Deliberative
Citizenship Initiative
→ https://www.davidsonday.org/student-life/community-and-culture

### "Individual activity, not a club" — VERIFIED

- **Longevity LKN** — a student-**founded**, student-run **501(c)(3) nonprofit**, not a
 school club. Free blood-pressure screenings across Lake Norman; founder Adam Rezai
 (junior), co-presidents Alexander Ajjan and Piper Pritchard. **Over 100 community members
 screened**, more than half showing high readings. Partnered with FeedNC. →
 https://www.davidsonday.org/p/~board/all-blogs/post/making-a-difference-one-conversation-at-a-time
- **AFAR archaeology** — **13 students** excavated the Adam Spach Rock House (Nov 2024)
 alongside five archaeologists from the Environmental Research Group; "first high school
 students to work on an archaeological site with the North Carolina State Historic
 Preservation Office." Parent liaisons Jim and Christy Pritchard. Whether this is a club or
 a program is **not defined** on the page. →
 https://www.davidsonday.org/p/~board/all-blogs/post/making-history-uncovering-history-davidson-day-afar-and-the-adam-spach-rock-house
- **Patriot Pals** — a peer-mentorship tradition, not a service club.

### Gap — 1b

No school-wide service-hours graduation requirement is published anywhere; the Upper School
page carries no service requirement.

**Davidson Day publishes no honor-society information of any kind.** Zero references to
National Honor Society, National Junior Honor Society, Cum Laude Society, National Art
Honor Society, Tri-M, Mu Alpha Theta, Beta Club, or any world-language honor society.

Pages checked with negative results:

- https://www.davidsonday.org/about/news-media/news and `/blog` — no induction stories at
 all; the only induction coverage on the whole site is the **Patriot Athletic Hall of
 Fame**, which is athletics rather than academic honors.

An independent web search for `"Davidson Day School" "National Honor Society" OR "Cum
Laude" induction` (2026-07-26) returned **no results for this school** — only other schools'
ceremonies and Davidson *College* (a different institution). The absence is therefore
corroborated off-site, not merely a fetching artifact.

### UNCONFIRMED third-party signal — deliberately not used

https://www.privateschoolreview.com/davidson-day-school-profile lists 17 extracurriculars
(Art Club, Battle of the Books, Chess Club, Community Service Club, Creative Writing Club,
Debate Club, Environmental Club, Film Club, Guitar Club, **Honor Council**, Math Olympiad,
Outdoors Club, Photography Club, Science Club, Student Ambassador Program, Student
Government Association) and enrollment of 572, PK–12. **"Honor Council" is a
disciplinary/integrity body, not an honor society.** None of this is corroborated on

sections.text:
- Issuu hosts the **2026-2027 Upper School Course Catalog**, the **2025-2026 catalogue**,
 and the **25-26 School Profile** — the documents most likely to name honor societies.
 Issuu's text-layer APIs return 403 AccessDenied and the HTML shell carries no extractable
 text, so their contents could **not** be verified. Confirmed again on 2026-07-26: no
 profile PDF is served from davidsonday.org itself (only images), so no local extraction
 was possible. A profile PDF obtained through a browser session remains the single
 highest-value follow-up for 1c.
- The site's search endpoint renders client-side only; no server-reachable JSON API exists.
- Five of the six "Learn More" cards on the Community and Culture page (Field Trips, Middle
 School Service Days, Patriot Pals, Social-Emotional Learning, Upper School Community
 Engagement Council) are **unlinked** — only Belonging has a live detail page. The card
 summaries quoted above are the full extent of published detail.
